title: Borel–Moore sections and integration
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum and geometric schemes of [sk-d-setup]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$. Work with a fixed geometric operation package [sk-d-six], on the ordinary small pro-etale derived categories $D(T,A)$ and their full subcategories $D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$. All inverse images below are derived. For a geometric scheme $a_T:T\to s$, let $A_T$ be its constant coefficient sheaf in degree zero [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and let $\omega_T\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ be the dualizing object supplied by the package. A Borel–Moore section on $T$ is a morphism $\alpha:A_T\to\omega_T$ in $D(T,A)$.

For a proper $s$-morphism $h:T\to T'$ between geometric schemes, put $a_T=a_{T'}h$. The proper map $h$ is compactifiable [def-nagata-compactifiable], using its factorization as the identity open immersion followed by $h$ itself. Write $c_h:h^*A_{T'}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T$ for the monoidal unit isomorphism, $P_h:Rh_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_!$ for the inverse of the package's proper comparison, and $d_h:h^!\omega_{T'}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_T$ for its dualizing-composition isomorphism. The unit $\eta_h$ of $h^*\dashv Rh_*$ is evaluated at $A_{T'}$; the counit $\varepsilon_h^!$ of the constructible adjunction $Rh_!\dashv h^!$ is evaluated at $\omega_{T'}$. Define the pushforward by the composite
$$
\begin{aligned}
h_*\alpha:\ A_{T'}&\xrightarrow{\eta_h}Rh_*h^*A_{T'}
\xrightarrow{Rh_*(c_h)}Rh_*A_T
\xrightarrow{Rh_*(\alpha)}Rh_*\omega_T\\
&\xrightarrow{P_h(\omega_T)}Rh_!\omega_T
\xrightarrow{Rh_!(d_h^{-1})}Rh_!h^!\omega_{T'}
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_h^!(\omega_{T'})}\omega_{T'}.
\end{aligned}
$$
These are precisely the adjunction and comparison components of [sk-d-six]. Their constructible-domain conditions hold: $A_T$ is bounded constructible by [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible], has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$ since it is the tensor unit, and hence belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]; the package already places $\omega_T$ and $\omega_{T'}$ in these full subcategories. Thus every ambient section $\alpha$ is a morphism in the subcategory where the comparisons and exceptional counit are defined. No ambient unbounded exceptional adjunction is required.

If $T$ is proper over $s$, let $n_s:\omega_s\xrightarrow{\sim}A_s$ be the normalization of [sk-d-six] and form
$$
v_\alpha=n_s\circ(a_T)_*\alpha\ \in\operatorname{End}_{D(s,A)}(A_s).
$$
Read this endomorphism as the scalar $\int_T\alpha\in A$. Explicitly, the finite-coefficient point functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] is termwise sections and sends $A_s$ to $A[0]$. Its equivalence property [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] identifies this endomorphism group with $\operatorname{End}_{D(A\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})}(A[0])=A$. The scalar is $H^0(\operatorname{Fib}_s(v_\alpha))(1)$, with $H^0$ as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This is the meaning of $\int_T\alpha=(a_T)_*\alpha$ through $\omega_s\simeq A_s$.
